1,505 rows: 20 chapters, 221 sub-chapters and 1,264 disease codes · Canada, both sexes, all ages · 2000–2024 · no filters or exclusions

All chapters, sub-chapters and disease codes: death counts and age-standardized rates

Every row in the source Statistics Canada cause-of-death tables, in its place in the ICD-10 hierarchy. Each row shows the annual death count and the age-standardized rate per 100,000 for every year from 2000 to 2024, with no statistics or models added. Open and close chapters, filter by level, search, or switch to a flat sortable list.

What is in the table
  • No restrictions. Nothing has been removed: all 20 chapters are included, with no minimum-deaths filter, Chapter II in full (malignant, in situ, benign and uncertain-behaviour neoplasms), and Chapter XXII with the provisional COVID-19 codes (U-codes).
  • Levels. Chapter rows are not in the source tables, so each is the sum of its top-level sub-chapters. Sub-chapter rows are ICD-10 code ranges (blocks and sub-blocks). Disease code rows are single ICD-10 codes (e.g. I21 or C34).
  • Counts are annual deaths, all ages, both sexes, Canada, including deaths with age not stated. Rates are directly age-standardized to the 2019 Canadian population (per 100,000): each year's age-specific rates, in 19 age bands (0–4 and 90+ combined), are weighted by 2019 population. Deaths with age not stated cannot be placed in an age band, so they are in the counts but not in the rates.
  • Columns. 2020–24 columns are shaded. 2020–24 avg is the plain average of those five years. Collapse 2000–19 replaces the twenty earlier years with their plain average. Blank cells mean no figure was published for that year (for example codes that did not exist yet or were retired); a zero is a published zero. 2024 figures are preliminary.
  • Duplicates. B99 and F99 each appear twice in the source under different names, with identical figures; both rows are kept.
  • Views. Hierarchy keeps the chapter → sub-chapter → code structure; click a row with a chevron to open or close it. Any level filter or search shows matching rows with their parents. Flat list shows rows without nesting and lets you sort: click any column header (clicking one from the hierarchy switches to the flat list).
